name: Catchment and Landscape Nature Recovery Grants
summary: Mid Suffolk grants for collaborative landscape-scale nature recovery projects across river catchments, including natural flood management, water quality work and priority habitat or species measures.
reporting: grantees must provide monitoring information to demonstrate the impact and benefits delivered to communities across Mid Suffolk

steps: Full application, if the Expression of Interest is supported
Full application scored against the grant matrix

eligibility.rule: Can obtain enough funding to cover the total project costs
Show financial viability with audited or independently examined accounts, or a financial business strategy
Has safeguarding, health and safety, and equal opportunities policies
Own the land, have at least 10 years left on the lease, or have written agreement from all participating landowners
Supports at least one BAP priority habitat or species
Supports at least one Suffolk LNRS aim or ambition
Addresses both flood management and water quality

applicant_types.quote: Eligible groups include (but are not limited to): town and parish councils village hall or playing field management committees sports clubs and centres charities social enterprises community shops and pubs community interest companies

geography.quote: Through our Community Grants team, grants are available for projects that deliver clear community benefits within Mid Suffolk.

access.quote: Applicants are required to submit an Expression of Interest prior to submitting a full application, as part of a two-stage application process.

window.quote: The Fund is currently closed for Expressions of Interest and Applications. The next application window will be open from 1 February 2027 to 30 April 2027.

amount.quote: Grants of between £50,000 and £200,000 can be applied for towards revenue, capital or pre-project costs or activities.

co_finance_required.quote: Match funding is not essential, though is encouraged as it is likely to form part of the project.

reporting.quote: For each of our Community Grants, we collect monitoring information from organisations awarded funding, in order to demonstrate the impact that our funding has had and the benefits delivered to communities across Mid Suffolk.

effort.quote: Applicants are first required to submit an Expression of Interest Form prior to submitting a full application.
The following application window will be open from 1st February 2027 to 30th April 2027.
All applications will be scored against a published Catchment and Landscape Nature Recovery Grant Scoring Matrix.

eligibility.quote: Applications for grants will only be considered from constituted Voluntary, Community, Faith and Social Enterprise (VCFSE) organisations which:
Are capable of obtaining from its own funds or other sources sufficient funding to cover the total project costs
Are financially viable, as evidenced by audited, independently examined accounts or financial business strategy.
Have Child and Adult Safeguarding, Health and Safety and Equal Opportunities policies for employees, volunteers and attendees

Own the land to which the application relates (freehold) Have a lease agreement with at least 10 years remaining (leasehold) Have written confirmation that all participating landowners agree to the proposed project
All applications will be required to support at least one of the key habitats and/or species identified by the Mid Suffolk Biodiversity Action Plan (BAP).
All applications will be required to support delivery of at least one of the Suffolk Local Nature Recovery Strategy (LNRS)'s aims and ambitions:
All applications must address flood management and water quality.
